properties.project_name: 1215 Michigan St -- proposed data center (adjacent to Potrero Power Station)
properties.digitized_from: The real DataSF Assessor parcel for blklot 4241004 (1215 Michigan St, 4.07 acres, zoned PDR-1-G), fetched directly from the DataSF Socrata API (data.sfgov.org/resource/acdm-wktn.json, dataset 'Parcels - Active and Retired') on 2026-09-21. Routed through this table, not status.csv, only because the parcel sits just south of data/raw/parcels.geojson's cached bounding box (src/config.py's BBOX_SOUTH=37.7545; this parcel's northern edge is ~37.7542) and so isn't in that local extract -- the polygon itself is the real, unmodified Assessor shape, not hand-traced or approximated. A small blklot 4241003 (~0.25 acres) immediately west, also addressed 1215 Michigan St, is not included: the Chronicle's reporting and the Assessor's own lot_area (177,223 sq ft = 4.07 acres) both point to 4241004 as 'the' 4-acre parcel in question.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL Assessor parcel geometry (not approximate), but the local basemap (data/raw/parcels.geojson, buildings.geojson) was fetched to an older, slightly smaller bounding box that stops just north of this parcel, so the grey basemap land/building texture is blank immediately around this shape on the map -- cosmetic only; the parcel's own outline and position are exact. Fix: widen src/config.py's BBOX_SOUTH and re-fetch the raw layers. That this is a real Assessor parcel rests on DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn), which lists blklot 4241004 as an active parcel addressed 1215 MICHIGAN; the Chronicle article names the address but does not discuss the parcel.
properties.notes: Sheedy Drayage, a crane rental and heavy-hauling company, currently operates on the site under owner R.P. Stagg & Co. LLC (as reported by the San Francisco Chronicle; not independently confirmed against a Recorder deed). The Chronicle reported in Sept 2026 that the exact status of any proposal was unclear and that no plans for a data center appeared to have been filed with the city -- see the record file for what's sourced about the proposal itself. Status is 'existing': the site is an operating industrial yard today, and a data center is only a reported possibility, not a plan of record. Use is 'industrial' for the same reason (the Chronicle describes a crane-rental and heavy-hauling yard); on the map it shows under Other, not as a commercial data center.
